exposure: baby size (very large or smaller than average)
cohort: The study included ever-married women from Demographic and Health Survey Data across nine developing countries in South and South-East Asia.
finding: The overall C-section prevalence across the nine South and South-East Asian countries was 13% (19% for institutional births), with a significant inclination towards caesarean delivery observed among urban women compared to rural women.
mod_finding: Caesarean delivery was primarily associated with urban women, those with very large or smaller than average baby sizes, women with a higher level of education, and deliveries occurring in private medical institutions.
country: Vietnam, India, Maldives, Timor-Leste, Nepal, Indonesia, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Cambodia
birth_weight: Categorical (very large or smaller than average baby sizes)
